newsitem.title: USA: OLYMPICS-SALT LAKE CITY GAMES BOSS THOMAS WELCH RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SALT LAKE CITY GAMES BOSS THOMAS WELCH RESIGNS.

text.p: Thomas Welch resigned as president of the chief executive officer of the Salt Lake Olympic Organising Committee Tuesday, eight days after being charged with domestic violence.
Welch, the man credited with bringing the Winter Olympics to Utah, announced his resignation at a news conference.

Welch, 52, faces a misdemeanor charge of domestic violence battery for allegedly getting into a scuffle with his wife, Alma, during an argument last month. According to a police report, the alleged dispute was over letters and gifts involving an unidentified women.
Welch denied the allegations and is scheduled to be arraigned on August 28.

Welch, an attorney, spearheaded the campaign to bring the Winter Olympics to Salt Lake City. Utah lost out to Nagano, Japan, for the 1998 Games before landing the 2002 Games. He was named president and chief executive of the organising committee in 1995.
The Salt Lake Organising Committee is scheduled to meet Wednesday and will likely consider a successor to Welch.
